speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any fluctuation in your symptoms, such as your double vision or weakness worsening towards the end of the day or after prolonged activity?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty swallowing, speaking, or breathing that worsens as the day progresses? I also need to check if your eyelids droop, especially after looking up for a while.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing, speaking, or shortness of breath, particularly later in the day? I would also like to observe your eyelids to see if they droop after you look upward for a period of time.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any drooping of your eyelids, particularly after looking upward for a period of time? I would also like to request a test to check for specific antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: RESULTS: Presence of ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze. Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of acetylcholine receptor antibodies and ptosis that worsens with sustained gaze confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
